hypothesis: Oceanic islands, though species-poor, have a much higher proportion of endemic native vascular plant species than area-matched mainland regions, often exceeding a fifth of their flora.
pass_criterion: Using GIFT, for oceanic (volcanic-origin, never land-connected) islands with at least 20 native vascular plant species: (a) the median endemic proportion (endemic species / native species) is at least 0.15, AND (b) it is at least 3 times the median endemic proportion of mainland regions in the same area bins (log10 area bins of width 1), AND (c) at least 25% of oceanic islands have an endemic proportion of at least 0.30. All three must hold.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if the median oceanic-island endemic proportion is below 0.10, or is less than 1.5 times the area-bin-matched mainland median, or fewer than 10% of oceanic islands have an endemic proportion of at least 0.30. Results between these bounds are inconclusive.
interpretation: Darwin's 'oceanic islands' map onto GIFT island entries classed as oceanic (volcanic or other never-connected geology, e.g. Hawaii, Galapagos, St Helena, Canaries, Azores). 'Endemic species' means species restricted to that island or archipelago unit, taken from GIFT's endemic-to-region flags or checklist endemism status. 'Number of kinds of inhabitants is scanty' means low native richness; 'extremely large' proportion is relative to area-matched mainland units. The test uses vascular plants only, since GIFT covers plants, whereas Darwin also discussed birds, insects and land shells. This is a modern reinterpretation of his broader claim, but it is within its scope because he cited plants such as the floras of St Helena and the Galapagos. The causal explanation about colonists being liable to modification is not tested.

dataset.name: GIFT
dataset.publisher: University of Göttingen (Biodiversity, Macroecology and Biogeography group), Global Inventory of Floras and Traits
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT is a global database of regional plant checklists. It records native species richness and endemic species counts per geographic unit, and it includes island-geology classes (oceanic vs continental) and area. The R package 'GIFT' exposes these through an API. Fields to use: entity_ID, entity_class, geo_entity_ref, area, native species counts and endemic counts (GIFT_checklist_conditional or GIFT_richness, with endemic_ref), and the island geology/type field in GIFT_env. The landing page itself is only an interactive map with a 'Taxon' filter, so the data pull would go through the API or R package.
